alt: Three themes, from Identity and Culture to Current and Future Study and Employment, feed both papers. Paper 1 (Reading, Grammar and Meaning) and Paper 2 (Writing) are each 1 hour 45 minutes, 70 marks and 50%; there is no listening or speaking.
caption: Two equal papers, both built on the same three themes.

after: ## The theme and how it is assessed
alt: Theme 1 Identity and Culture branches into three topics: 1.1 family, friends and people I know (two relationship sub-topics), 1.2 technology in everyday life (social media, mobile technology) and 1.3 free-time activities (music, cinema and TV, sport, customs and festivals).
caption: Eight sub-topics give the contexts; the papers test your Urdu, not cultural knowledge.

alt: A large circle of passive vocabulary (words you recognise) contains a smaller circle of active vocabulary (words you can produce). Recognition is enough for Paper 1 Reading; Paper 2 Writing can only use active vocabulary.
caption: Recognition alone will carry you through reading but fail you in writing.

alt: A four-step staircase: a simple statement, then an opinion, then a reason, then an example, each step higher. Range is widened further with three tenses, comparatives, connectives and time markers.
caption: Adding a reason and an example is the most reliable way to move up a band.

alt: For reading, first decide whether the question wants a detail, an opinion (look for evaluative language) or an inference. For writing, check that every bullet point is addressed, opinions have reasons and tenses are varied.
caption: Name the question type in reading; cover every bullet in writing.

alt: A weak festival answer lists what happens in one tense with no opinion or reason. A strong one moves through past, present and future, gives an opinion with a reason and adds a personal detail.
caption: Three tenses, an opinion, a reason and a personal detail make a top-band answer.
